tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). description: "Maester Packs (third-party pack + connector marketplace) design — where the draft and mockup live, owner rulings, and what is still open"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project

Drafted 2026-10-07 in worktree `.claude/worktrees/maester-3-planning-6643a9`: `docs/proposals/maester-packs-design.md`, on branch `claude/maester-packs-design`, draft PR maester365/maester#2358 stacked on the 3.0 branch (#2334); retarget to main after 3.0 merges. Site mockup canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/9frFAaGEGJgDRXvyst8Ht1 (private).

Owner rulings (2026-10-07): names **pack** / **Maester Packs**; domain **packs.maester.dev** (maester.dev DNS is on Cloudflare); site + small Worker API (+ D1) on Cloudflare, indexing/scanning in GitHub Actions on a public repo (free minutes), keep costs ~$0–5/month; **binaries allowed** but flagged High risk (risk levels Low/Medium/High/Blocked, like skills.sh audits); **v1 runs packs in-process** (isolation via containers later; keep the hosted-service angle generic in public docs); **no verification programme in v1** — badges instead: Official, Microsoft MVP (from the MVP directory API the `merill/newsletter` repo syncs, `app/src/lib/server/authors/mvp-api.ts`), GitHub-verified org. Publisher-side scanners (Codacy/CodeRabbit) shown only as "repository signals".

Design review of 2026-10-07 fully folded in (fork-commit reachability, single loader gate, packs can't pose as built-ins, namespaced connector services `<CODE>.<Platform>`, -IncludePackScopes/MissingScope, phase-1 blocklist with serial/expiry/offline root key, split scan/publish indexer, **no archive mirror (Merill ruled: never cache repos in Cloudflare; a pack gone from GitHub is skipped — NotRun `PackUnavailable` + report warning)**, lifecycle states, numeric IDs, ID ledger, pack API contract, AllSigned/WDAC, terms/takedowns, /p/ routes, maester365 code `MAES`).

**Why:** Merill wants to review the full design before implementation.

Pack test IDs are `MP.<code>.<number>` (e.g. MP.CNT.0001): `MP.` reserved prefix, 2–5 char code (letters/digits, starts with a letter) held by the **publisher (GitHub user/org, numeric owner ID)**, claimed at the first index of any of its repos, first come first served — no PR; one code per owner, permanent, shared by all its packs (index keeps IDs unique across them); every not-listed version gets an indexing status with reason + fix (doc 7.7, packs.maester.dev/status/{owner}/{repo}, Test-MtPack -Remote); `Find-MtPack -Code` / packs.maester.dev/codes/<CODE> lookup; anti-squat: account >30 days, one claim/day, unlisted claims lapse after 90 days. Also ruled: list on first passing install (owner account >30 days), **one new pack per owner per day**, Astro, High-risk packs shown by default, MVP API best-effort, first official pack Google Workspace.

**Under discussion (2026-10-08, community feedback from TestimoX and LeastPrivilegedMSGraph; NOT yet in the design doc — Merill wants the doc updated only after the Discord discussion ends):** outside tools run as their own step and the pack's connector only reads the output file (no signing; schema-version + max-age checks); **hybrid module-backed packs** (code in the publisher's PowerShell module, pack = manifest + build-generated static catalog + docs, `RequiresModules` + `Provider {Module, ApiVersion}`; chosen over Gallery-hosted packs so GitHub/MVP badges still validate); Maester never installs modules (generated `Install-Module` command; missing → tests skipped); publisher Setup tab; rule catalogs; coverage as own result (`NotCollected`, opt-in CI); own auth libs wrapped as connectors + run-scoped cache; permissions beyond Graph (Entra/Azure RBAC/Exchange roles, `MissingPermission`); connection targets via `Connections.<Service>`/parameter kinds/families. Mode names proposed: code = **Script pack** / **Module pack**; data = **Live** / **Import** / **Collect** (optional Collect hook once per run + Release hook, off by default). Summarised (with two SVG diagrams) in the overview HTML's "Under discussion" section.

**How to apply:** Only owner-side setup is still open (GitHub App, signing key, Cloudflare). Never raise or record the existing `InvokeMaester` PostHog run telemetry in the Packs design — Merill ruled it out of scope (opt-out is already documented). Don't implement until he rules. Keep maester-cloud internals out of public docs, as with [[maester-3-design]].

  ## Findings: Maester Packs login and how maester.dev uses data
  
  ### 0. Which repo is which
  - **/Users/merill/github/maester-cloud-packs** is the packs site and API that is in use now. Its remote is `https://github.com/jozrahq/maester-cloud-packs`. The checked-out branch is `feat/catalog-json`, last commit a19cf54 on 2026-11-08.
  - **/Users/merill/github/maester-packs** is not the packs site. It is another checkout of `maester365/maester`, with several fork remotes. Its branch is `claude/project-thread-adkkqb` and its last commit is from 2026-10-23.
  - **Design doc:** it is not in `docs/proposals/` on the current branch. It exists only on branch `origin/claude/maester-packs-design` (a12ea5ac0, 2026-10-08) as `docs/proposals/maester-packs-design.md`, next to `maester-packs-overview.html`. Read it with `git show origin/claude/maester-packs-design:docs/proposals/maester-packs-design.md`.
    - The doc says the domain will be **packs.maester.dev** (§2, lines 72-92; §8). What was built is **packs.maester.cloud**.
  - **Other pack branches:** `worktree-scubagear-pack`, plus remote branches `claude/pack-registry`, `codex/pack-security-boundaries`, `packs-guide`, `packs-publish-docs`, `zta-pack-banner` and `zta-pack-readme`.
  - **Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/scubagear-pack/docs/proposals/` holds `packs-any-language.md` and `zero-trust-assessment-pack.md`.
  
  ### 1. Packs site and API (maester-cloud-packs)
  The README.md (lines 1-15) describes the layout:
  - `data/`: seed lists and sample data
  - `indexer/`: `Invoke-PackIndex.ps1`, which scans packs with Maester's own checks
  - `site/`: the static Astro site
  - `worker/`: the Cloudflare Worker
  
  **Stack and hosting**
  - **Site:** Astro 5.18.2 with `output: 'static'` (`site/astro.config.mjs`). It is served as static assets of a Cloudflare Worker.
  - **Main Worker** (`worker/wrangler.toml`):
    - Name `maester-packs`, flag `nodejs_compat`, custom domain `packs.maester.cloud`.
    - Assets come from `../site/dist`, with `run_worker_first = ["/api/*", "/mcp", "/oauth/*", "/.well-known/oauth-*", ...]`.
    - Storage: a D1 binding `DB` (database `maester-packs`), Analytics Engine `RUNS`, Pipelines→R2 `RUN_STREAM`, two rate limiters, and a daily cron `17 3 * * *`.
    - Vars: `SITE_URL = "https://packs.maester.cloud"` and `ADMIN_GITHUB_IDS = "1288081"`.
  - **Telemetry Worker:** a second Worker, `maester-api` (`worker/wrangler.api.toml`), on `api.maester.dev`. It serves only `POST /v1/telemetry` and `POST /v1/events`, and uses the same D1 database.
    - Maester calls it from `powershell/internal/session/Write-Telemetry.ps1:68`.
    - Maester's blocklist URL is `https://packs.maester.cloud/blocklist.json`, set in `powershell/assets/MaesterPackTrust.json:4`.
  - **Deploy:** the GitHub Actions workflow `index.yml` runs every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`). It scans packs, then writes the `listings` and `deploy` branches. Cloudflare Workers Builds deploys the `deploy` branch (README "Deploying").
  - **Dependency:** the Worker's only dependency is `better-auth` 1.7.7 (`worker/package.json`).
  
  **DB schema** (`worker/schema.sql`, every table):
  - **Telemetry:** `installs`, `networks`, `queue`, `runs`, `pack_runs`, `run_networks` (lines 5-67).
  - **Daily totals:** `daily_events`, `daily_errors`, `daily_places`, `daily_platforms`, `daily_active`, `daily_versions`, `daily_packs` (lines 76-157).
  - **Better Auth:** `"user"`, `"session"`, `"account"`, `"verification"` (lines 160-205).
  - **Admin and registry:**
    - `site_admins(github_id, login, added_by, added_at)` (line 208)
    - `site_lists(list, key, value JSON, updated_at, updated_by)`: holds the lists `reserved`, `blocklist`, `official`, `featured`, `hidden` and `unlisted` (line 217)
    - `pack_registry(guid PK, code UNIQUE, pack_id, owner_id, owner_login, source, registered_at, registered_by, updated_at)` (line 229)
    - `publish_requests` (line 243)
    - `admin_log(at, github_id, login, action, detail)` (line 252)
  - **MCP OAuth:** `oauth_clients`, `oauth_codes`, `oauth_tokens`, `mcp_drafts`, `mcp_draft_images` (lines 262-304).
  
  **API routes** (router in `worker/src/index.ts:61-95`):
  - **Sign-in:** `/api/auth/*`, handled by Better Auth (line 64).
  - **Public and telemetry:**
    - `POST /api/v1/events`
    - `GET /api/v1/stats` (sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, index.ts:208)
    - `GET /api/v1/queue` (bearer key)
    - `POST /api/v1/telemetry`
    - `GET /api/v1/usage`
    - `GET /api/v1/report` and `GET /api/v1/history` (bearer `REPORT_KEY`)
  - **Site routes** (`worker/src/site.ts:31-76`):
    - Open: `GET /api/v1/codes`, `GET /api/v1/site-data`
    - Signed in: `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/repos`, `POST /api/v1/me/check`, `POST /api/v1/me/publish`, `GET /api/v1/me/packs`, `POST /api/v1/me/packs/hidden`
    - Admins only: `/api/v1/admin/{admins|unlisted|registry|reserved|blocklist|official|featured}` with GET/POST/DELETE
  - **Builder:** `/api/v1/builder/{config,pack,code,save,release,callback,disconnect}` (`worker/src/builder/routes.ts`).
  - **MCP server:** `/mcp` (`worker/src/mcp/server.ts`) with tools get_pack, check_code, create_pack, update_manifest, update_guide, add_test, upload_image, make_banner, validate, save and release.
  - **MCP OAuth 2.1 + PKCE:** `/oauth/register|authorize|token` and `/.well-known/oauth-*` (`worker/src/mcp/oauth.ts:34-50`).
  - **Static JSON from the site build:** `index.json`, `codes.json`, `blocklist.json`, and `catalog.json` (`site/src/pages/catalog.json.ts`: each listed pack with its tests).
  
  ### 2. How sign-in works on packs
  **Library and provider:** Better Auth, with a GitHub **OAuth App** (not a GitHub App) as the only provider. Config is in `worker/src/auth.ts:9-47`:
  ```ts
  betterAuth({ appName: 'Maester Packs', baseURL: env.SITE_URL || origin, basePath: '/api/auth',
    secret: env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, database: env.DB, trustedOrigins: [env.SITE_URL || origin],
    socialProviders: { github: { clientId, clientSecret, scope: ['read:org'],
      mapProfileToUser: (profile) => ({ githubLogin: profile.login }) } },
    user: { additionalFields: { githubLogin: { type: 'string', required: false, input: false } } },
    account: { encryptOAuthTokens: true },
    session: { expiresIn: 60*60*24*14, updateAge: 60*60*24 },
    advanced: { cookiePrefix: 'packs', useSecureCookies: ..., defaultCookieAttributes: { sameSite: 'lax', httpOnly: true, path: '/' } } })
  ```
  - **Scopes:** `read:user`, `user:email` and `read:org`.
  - **Callback:** `https://packs.maester.cloud/api/auth/callback/github` (README "Setting it up" step 7). The README says why it is an OAuth App: "an App's user token only sees repositories where it is installed".
  - **Cookie:** host-only, with no Domain attribute, so it goes only to packs.maester.cloud (auth.ts:2-3).
  - **Write protection:** every write must carry an `Origin` header that equals `SITE_URL` (`site.ts:38`, `sameOrigin` at :78).
  - **No CORS on `/api/v1/me*`.** The CSP has `connect-src 'self'` (`site/public/_headers`).
  
  **Client side:**
  - Sign-in is `POST /api/auth/sign-in/social {provider:'github', callbackURL}`, for example `site/src/pages/account.astro:88` and `site/src/lib/publish-page.ts:51`.
  - Sign-out is `POST /api/auth/sign-out`.
  - `GET /api/v1/me` returns `{signedIn, login, name, image, githubId, admin}` (`site.ts:41-43`).
  - The header remembers the account in localStorage key `maesterpacks.me` (`site/public/account-boot.js`, `Base.astro:128`).
  
  **What is stored about a user** (`schema.sql:160-169`): `user(id, name, email UNIQUE, emailVerified, image, createdAt, updatedAt, githubLogin)`.
  - The `account` row holds `accountId` (the GitHub numeric ID) and the encrypted GitHub access and refresh tokens.
  - The session object (`auth.ts:49-78`) is `Viewer {userId, githubId, login, name, image, admin, accountRowId}`. `githubId` is read from `account.accountId` where `providerId='github'`.
  
  **Roles:**
  - **Admin** = a GitHub ID in `ADMIN_GITHUB_IDS` (merill, 1288081) or in the `site_admins` table (`auth.ts:80-88`).
  - There are no other user roles.
  - A "publisher" is not a role. The Worker checks it per repository by calling GitHub with the user's token: the repo must have `permissions.admin`, be public, not a fork, and the owner account must be at least 30 days old (`site.ts:125-185`).
  - Pack badges come from the indexer, not from sign-in (`indexer/PackIndex.Helpers.ps1:151-156`):
    - `BuiltIn`
    - `Official` (from the `official` list; seed `data/seed/official.json` = `maester365/maester`)
    - `VerifiedOrganization` (GitHub `is_verified`)
  - `site/src/components/Badges.astro:3` has a label for `MVP: 'Microsoft MVP'`, but nothing produces an MVP badge. The design doc §9.5 planned a weekly sync from the MVP directory.
  
  **What a signed-in user can do:**
  - List their public repos where they are an admin.
  - Check and publish a pack. Publishing registers its Guid and Code to the GitHub owner ID for good.
  - See My Packs and their usage.
  - Hide or show their own pack.
  - Use the Builder at /build.
    - The Builder is a second GitHub App, "Maester Packs Builder", with no private key.
    - Its user token lasts 8 hours and is sealed in the HttpOnly cookie `__Host-mpb` (`worker/src/builder/connect.ts:1-40`).
  - Use the MCP server.
  - Admins can also manage the lists, the registry, unlisting and other admins.
  - "Claim a code": there is no claim flow. A code is registered on first Publish. Reserved codes are handed out by an admin on request through a `pack-report` issue (`site.ts:22`; `site/src/pages/codes/index.astro`).
  
  ### 3. Voting, rating, comments or feedback
  - **Packs site and worker:** none. A grep for vote, rating, comment and feedback finds nothing.
  - **Ranking:** only installs and active-use counts (`/api/v1/stats`). The design doc §7.3 also ranks by installs and trending.
  - **Pack reports:** made through GitHub issues with the `pack-report` label (README "Reporting a pack"). **That label is not in `.github/labels.json`** (0 matches).
  - **maester.dev:** no voting, comments, giscus or sign-in. The only "rating" hit is `ratingOrder` in `website/src/components/catalog/data.ts:10`, which orders the Low/Medium/High values of the cost and impact filters.
  
  ### 4. How maester.dev gets its data
  - **Hosting:** fully static.
    - Astro 7.4.4 with Starlight 0.42.8 and `@astrojs/react`. There is no adapter and no `output` setting (`website/astro.config.mjs`), and no `functions/` folder.

  - **Other GitHub pieces:** a separate "Maester Packs Builder" GitHub App, and an MCP server with its own OAuth 2.1 (`worker/src/mcp/oauth.ts`).

  - **No shared identity with Maester Cloud.** maester-cloud has zero references to packs.

  - Any roadmap/vote/claim-to-implement concept for Maester tests or the open-source project. The roadmap is Maester Cloud product-only, and there is no "claim" or assignee field.

content.text:
My recommendation: build the ideas board on the Maester Packs stack with GitHub sign-in, keep it separate from the Maester Cloud roadmap store, and connect the two by links and an optional account link. Opening Maester Cloud sign-up to everyone is worth doing, but as its own project, not as the way into this feature.

## What exists today

| | maester.dev | Maester Packs | Maester Cloud roadmap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hosting | Static Astro on Cloudflare Pages | Cloudflare Worker + D1 | Azure Functions and Container Apps, Azure Table Storage |
| Sign-in | None | GitHub, through Better Auth | Entra External ID, email and password only |
| Who can sign up | n/a | Anyone with a GitHub account | Paying customers and invited members only |
| Voting and comments | None | None | Votes, suggestions and comments for customers; operators curate features |
| Status | Live | Live | Dev ring only; `/roadmap` returns 404 in prod |

Three facts shape the design:

- **Cloud sign-up is closed on purpose.** A sign-up extension rejects any email that is not a customer or invitee, and the portal API accepts tokens only from its own app and origin.
- **Cloud has one entitlement rule, not per-feature gating.** Every portal endpoint assumes a signed-in person is a paying customer. There is no free tier.
- **The community is already keyed by GitHub handle.** All 893 tests carry `Author`, the contributor registry marks maintainers and MVPs, and CODEOWNERS names the suite teams.

## Recommended design

**Identity: GitHub, the same accounts as Packs.**
- Reuse the Packs Better Auth setup and its D1 user table, matched on GitHub numeric ID.
- Serve the API from a Worker route on `maester.dev/api/...`, so the static site calls it same-origin with a host-only cookie.
- This needs a second GitHub OAuth App, because an OAuth App has one callback URL. It should request `read:user` only.

**Store: D1 for ideas, GitHub issues for the work.**
- Ideas, votes and comments live in D1.
- When a maintainer accepts an idea, the Worker creates a linked issue in `maester365/maester`. From then on the issue is the record of the work.
- I chose this over plain GitHub Discussions because Discussions cannot show role badges, structured test fields (product, suite, control) or roadmap statuses.

**Idea lifecycle.**
- Kinds: new test, change to an existing test, feature, pack, docs.
- Statuses: New → Under review → Accepted → Claimed → In review → Shipped, plus Declined and Duplicate.
- Claiming assigns the GitHub issue and reserves the MT number. A claim lapses after about 30 days without a pull request.
- An idea about an existing test links to its ID, so the catalog page for that test can list its open ideas.

**Roles are derived, never self-declared.**

| Badge | Source |
|---|---|
| Core maintainer | `maintainer: true` in the contributor registry, or the maester365 team |
| Suite owner | CODEOWNERS teams (`core-tests`, `eidsca`, `cisa`) |
| Test author | The test's `Author` attribute, shown on ideas linked to that test |
| Contributor, MVP, Sponsor | Existing contributor and sponsor data |
| Maester Cloud customer | Optional account link (below) |

There is no per-test "owner" field today, only `Author` and `Contributor`. I would start with `Author` and add an owner override only if authors turn out to be absent.

**Votes: one person, one vote, with a breakdown.**
- I recommend against weighting paid votes. On an open-source board it reads as pay-to-win and contradicts "Maester is free" on the pricing page.
- Instead, show the tally by segment (for example "42 votes, 6 from Cloud customers, 3 from sponsors") and let maintainers sort by segment. You get the signal without the optics.
- Customers keep exclusive influence over the Cloud product roadmap, which the pricing already promises.

**Moderation.** Reuse the Packs rules (account older than 30 days, rate limits, admin log) and the Cloud hide reasons, with post-moderation.

## Integrating with the Maester Cloud roadmap

Do not merge the stores. Cloud's tables are keyed by External ID identities, have strict privacy rules (customer identity never leaves Kermit), and are duplicated across three planes.

- **First:** maester.dev gets a roadmap page for the open-source project, with a Maester Cloud tab built from Cloud's public `GET /api/roadmap` at build time. This needs the Cloud roadmap live in prod.
- **Next:** an operator can link a Cloud suggestion about checks or the engine to a community idea. This fits the untracked work-tracking proposal that makes GitHub issues the system of record.
- **Later:** "Connect GitHub" in the Cloud portal. It is opt-in and reveals only a "Maester Cloud customer" badge, no company name.

## Should anyone be able to sign into Maester Cloud?

Yes, eventually, and it matches your goal of free core building blocks with paid features. But it is a bigger change than the ideas board:

1. Replace the single entitlement rule with a feature-to-plan map.
2. Add a free tier to the customer model.
3. Then relax the sign-up gate and add abuse controls.

Doing step 3 first would give free accounts whatever the portal currently assumes every identity may do. If the ideas board stores linked identities (GitHub required, Cloud optional), it will not need rework when this lands.

## Phases

1. Board on maester.dev: sign-in, ideas, votes, comments, badges, promote to issue.
2. Claims, MT reservation, ideas on catalog pages, the open-source roadmap page.
3. Cloud tab and account linking.
4. Cloud free tier and open sign-up (separate project in the cloud repo).

## Decisions for you

- **Vote weighting:** segments instead of weights, as above, or real weights.
- **Where the backend code lives:** the Packs Worker repo is private (`jozrahq`). Reusing it is fastest; a public repo is better for community trust in the voting.
- **Test owner:** `Author` to start, or a new `Owner` attribute now.

# Design: Community ideas and roadmap

> **Status: DRAFT for owner review. Nothing is implemented.** Drafted 2026-11-09.
> Section 11 lists the decisions that are still open. This document covers the
> open-source project only. Maester Cloud has its own product roadmap for its
> customers; section 9 says how the two connect, and nothing here changes how Maester
> Cloud works.

## 1. Summary

Anyone in the community can propose a test, a feature, a pack or a documentation
change on maester.dev, vote and comment on other people's ideas, and take an accepted
idea and implement it. Maintainers triage ideas into a public roadmap. A person's
standing in the project (core maintainer, suite owner, author of the test under
discussion, contributor, sponsor) is shown beside what they write.

The design in one page:

- **Sign in with GitHub**, the same way Maester Packs does. The project already knows
  its community by GitHub handle: every built-in test names its `Author`, the

repository moves the idea to In review when a pull request references the issue and to
Shipped when it merges. An existing issue can also be attached to an idea, so the
backlog does not have to be re-entered.

The roadmap page shows Accepted, Claimed, In review and Shipped ideas, grouped as
Planned, In progress and Shipped by release. It is built from the same tables; there
is no second list to maintain.

Each test's page in the catalog lists the open ideas linked to it.

## 6. Claiming an idea

- Only Accepted ideas can be claimed, one claimer at a time.
- Claiming assigns the GitHub issue to the claimer. For a `test` idea it also reserves
  the next MT number, replacing the manual comment on issue 697.
- A claim lapses after 30 days with no linked pull request. The claimer gets a
  reminder a week before, and can extend once.
- A maintainer can release any claim.

## 7. Roles and badges

Badges are derived, and shown beside the person's name on ideas and comments.

| Badge | Source |
|---|---|
| Core maintainer | `maintainer: true` in the contributor registry |
| Suite owner | Membership of a CODEOWNERS team, shown on ideas in that suite |
| Test author | The `Author` of the test an idea is linked to, shown on that idea only |
| Contributor | Has a merged contribution |
| Microsoft MVP | The contributor registry |
| Sponsor | GitHub Sponsors |

Maintainers can accept, decline, merge, hide and release claims. Suite owners can do
the same within their suite. Everyone else can propose, vote, comment and claim.

A comment from a maintainer, a suite owner or the test's author is marked as such and
can be pinned above the thread, so the people responsible for a test are easy to find
in a long discussion.

There is no per-test owner field today, only `Author` and `Contributor`. Version 1
uses `Author`. See section 11.3.

## 8. Voting

One vote per person per idea. The author votes for their own idea automatically.
Shipped and declined ideas take no more votes.

The tally shows the total and a breakdown: maintainers, contributors, sponsors and
others. Maintainers can sort by any group.

No group's vote counts for more than another's. A weighted vote on an open-source
board would mean influence can be bought, which is not what "Maester is free" says.
The breakdown gives maintainers the same signal.

## 9. Maester Cloud

Maester Cloud has a product roadmap of its own, for its customers. The two stay
separate: different products, different sign-ins, different audiences.

They connect in three ways, in this order:

1. **Links.** The maester.dev roadmap page links to the Maester Cloud roadmap, and the
   other way round.
2. **Shared ideas.** A customer suggestion that is really about a check or the engine
   can be linked to a community idea, so it is tracked once, in the open.
3. **Account link.** A Maester Cloud customer can choose to connect their GitHub
   account. Their votes are then counted in a "Maester Cloud customers" group in the
   breakdown, and they get a badge. It is opt-in and shows nothing about the customer
   but the badge.

## 10. Moderation and abuse

- A GitHub account must be at least 30 days old to propose, comment or claim, the
  rule Maester Packs uses for publishers.
- Rate limits per account on proposing, commenting and voting.
- Ideas and comments are visible at once and moderated afterwards. A hidden item
  records a reason: spam, off-topic, abusive, personal information, duplicate.
- Every moderation action is written to `admin_log`.
- The site's terms and code of conduct apply; the page links to both.

## 11. Open decisions

1. **Vote weighting.** This draft uses one person, one vote with a breakdown
   (section 8). The alternative is a real weight for some groups.
2. **Where the backend code lives.** Reusing the Maester Packs Worker and database is
   the least work and gives one account across both sites. A public repository of its
   own lets the community read the code that counts their votes.
3. **Test owner.** Version 1 treats a test's `Author` as its owner. If authors turn
   out to be absent, an owner override is needed: a new attribute, or a list kept
   beside the contributor registry.
4. **GitHub Discussions.** Existing idea discussions could be imported as ideas, or
   left where they are with a pointer to the new page.

## 12. Phases

1. **Board.** Sign-in, propose, vote, comment, badges, maintainer triage, accept to a
   GitHub issue.
2. **Implementing.** Claims, MT reservation, webhook status, ideas on catalog pages,
   the roadmap page.
3. **Maester Cloud.** Links, shared ideas, account link.

## 13. Not yet verified

- That a Worker route on `maester.dev/api/*` can sit in front of the Cloudflare Pages
  project as it is deployed today.
- That Better Auth can share a user table between two OAuth Apps on two hosts, if
  decision 11.2 goes that way.
- The cost at community scale; expected to stay inside the same few dollars a month as
  Maester Packs.

3:Three planes in one repo. The **repo root is the product** — the app, API, portal SPA, setup wizard, runner, PowerShell module, and customer infra that ship to customers. `website/` is the website plane (marketing site, founders portal + portal-api, signup API, all website Azure IaC). `kermit/` is the internal operator app. Each plane is self-contained: its own package manager roots, lockfiles, solution, and Aspire AppHost. Only `.github/workflows/` is shared.
4-
5:## The publish boundary
6-
7:Everything the root plane lists in [publish/manifest.txt](publish/manifest.txt) ships to customers as a snapshot of `jozralabs/maester-cloud` on every approved release ([publish-customer.yml](.github/workflows/publish-customer.yml)). That file is the boundary; treat edits near it as customer-facing releases:
8-
9-- Never add a `website/` or `kermit/` path to the manifest. Before adding ANY path, re-check everything it stages is customer-safe.
10:- Manifest-listed files must never contain the strings `kermit` or `jozrahq` — the publish job greps the staged tree and fails the release on a hit.
11:- The root [.dockerignore](.dockerignore) names `website`/`kermit` and is masked at publish by [publish/overlay/.dockerignore](publish/overlay/.dockerignore). If you change customer-relevant lines in the root file, mirror them in the overlay copy.
12-
13-## Toolchain isolation (do not "unify")
14-
15:Root `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `Directory.Packages.props` ship to customers, so `website/` and `kermit/` stay out of the root pnpm workspace, the root solution, and root CPM:
16-
17-- `website/Directory.Build.props` and `website/Directory.Packages.props` are inheritance barriers (the website codebase isn't built against the root's TreatWarningsAsErrors/CPM). Keep them.
18-- `kermit/Directory.Packages.props` pins kermit's packages (CPM nearest-wins); kermit otherwise inherits the root Build.props and global.json.
19-- `website/src` is npm (package-lock.json); `website/portal` is pnpm with its own workspace file. Those nested `pnpm-workspace.yaml` files stop pnpm's upward walk — keep them.
20-- `website/portal` consumes the shared design system through a one-way `"@maester-cloud/ui": "file:../../src/ui"` dependency — no root-plane file references `website/`. Its Docker image builds from the **repo-root** context with the allowlist in [website/portal-api/Dockerfile.dockerignore](website/portal-api/Dockerfile.dockerignore). After changing `src/ui` (its `package.json` especially), re-run `pnpm install` in `website/portal` so its lockfile and installed copy stay in sync — the image build's `--frozen-lockfile` fails otherwise.
21-
22-## CI/CD
23-
--
25:- Any push to main touching product paths (see the filter in [auto-release.yml](.github/workflows/auto-release.yml)) cuts a full dev release automatically. Docs, workflows, `publish/`, `website/`, and `kermit/` are outside the filter.
26:- Browser E2E: [tests/e2e](tests/e2e/README.md) (Playwright, against the app image + Azurite) gates every release before `promote-ppe`. A user-facing portal feature or fix ships with a spec there; it is a standalone pnpm package, deliberately outside the root workspace and the publish manifest.
27-- **Deploying a feature: use its runbook.** When asked how to deploy something, or for the next deploy steps, find its runbook under `website/deploy/runbooks/` (feature rollouts are indexed in that folder's README, e.g. `0006-onboarding-emails`) or `kermit/deploy/runbooks/`. Read its **Rollout status** table, then give the steps for the requested ring in runbook order, copying the runbook's commands (one command per `bash` block) rather than composing new ones. The founder runs every elevation, workflow dispatch and Azure write; you only run read-only checks. After a ring's step is done, update the status table in a PR. Before giving the steps for any website or Kermit ring deploy, read the Rollout status table of every feature runbook and include the steps still to do in that ring, in runbook order: infrastructure a new image needs comes before the image, and seed data such as `0008-public-roadmap` is part of the deploy.
28:- Website deploy config source of truth: `website/deploy/environments/{dev,ppe,prod}.json` (domains, resources, GitHub env names, FIC names). Kermit's is `kermit/deploy/environments/{dev,ppe,prod}.json` (own resource group per ring in the ring subscription; see [kermit/deploy/README.md](kermit/deploy/README.md)). The release pipeline itself: [docs/owner-setup-runbook.md](docs/owner-setup-runbook.md) §10.
29-
30-## Portal data scaling
31-
32:Portal pages must stay fast as tenants and runs grow. Before adding or changing a portal page, an `/api` read endpoint, or a background job that reads runs or results, read [docs/portal-read-model-design.md](docs/portal-read-model-design.md) and keep to its scaling rules:
33-
34-- A page load makes a fixed number of API requests; no loader loops over runs or tenants.
35-- Lists and summaries carry no result text; fetch it for one test on demand.
36-- Anything derived only from processed runs is computed when the run is processed, not per request.
37-- Policy, accepted risks and views are applied on read, never stored into a summary.
38-- No request path scans a table partition that grows with history; history is the trailing 120 days per tenant.
39-- Stored summaries hold facts, never a page's layout. A feature that needs a new stored fact says how past runs get it: forward only, backfill from rows, or backfill from reports.
40-- No new always-on Azure service.

content.text:
The Maester Packs site and API are in `/Users/merill/github/maester-cloud-packs`, a separate private repo (`jozrahq/maester-cloud-packs`), currently on branch `feat/catalog-json`. It is served at packs.maester.cloud.

| Folder | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `worker/` | The Cloudflare Worker: API routes, GitHub sign-in (`worker/src/auth.ts`), the D1 schema (`worker/schema.sql`), the pack Builder and the MCP server |
| `site/` | The static Astro site the Worker serves |
| `indexer/` | `Invoke-PackIndex.ps1`, which scans packs with Maester's own checks |
| `data/` | Seed lists and sample data |

Two other places are related:

- **The client side is in the open-source repo.** The commands that install and run packs are in `powershell/public/packs/` and `powershell/internal/packs/` in `/Users/merill/github/maester`, and the packs that ship with Maester are in `packs/` at its root.
- **`/Users/merill/github/maester-packs` is not the packs site.** Despite the name, it is another checkout of `maester365/maester`.

content.text:
Yes, I think the packs repo is the better home for this doc.

- **The code would land there.** The design reuses that repo's Worker, D1 database and GitHub sign-in, so the doc would sit next to what it describes.
- **It has nothing to do with the Maester Cloud codebase.** The cloud repo is the product, the customer portal and the operator app; the ideas board touches none of them.
- **It is still private.** The packs repo is under `jozrahq`, so the doc stays out of public view either way.

The one part that belongs in the cloud repo is the piece I left out: opening Maester Cloud sign-up, a free tier and per-feature tiers. That changes the cloud portal's access model and should be a separate doc there.

Moving it does not settle the open decision about where the backend code lives. If you later choose a public repo for the voting code, the doc would move with it.

Say the word and I'll move the commit to a local branch in `maester-cloud-packs` (it is on `feat/catalog-json`, so I'd use a separate worktree again) and delete the branch and worktree I made in `maester-cloud`.
